newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa still hopes for Fokker rescue.
newsitem.headline: Dasa still hopes for Fokker rescue.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), which holds an indirect stake in Fokker N.V., said on Thursday it hoped that the Dutch plane maker could still be saved but it was prepared for Fokker to be wound up.

Court-appointed Dutch administrators rated the chances of Fokker's survival as "minimal" after Bombardier unit Shorts pulled out of delivering wings for Fokker aircraft, leading rescue talks with Samsung Aerospace to fail.
Asked whether Dasa was prepared for Fokker to fail, a company spokesman said: "We have naturally calculated the impact...we would wish for a positive outcome."

The spokesman declined to make any further comment, but confirmed Dasa had exercised a three-year-old option to buy all outstanding shares from the Dutch government in Fokker Holding, which now has a minority stake in operating company Fokker N.V.
Dasa also supplies fuselages for Fokker aircraft.
Dutch administrators said that Fokker would continue to make aircraft already ordered by KLM, Cityhopper, Vietnam Airlines and Ethiopian Airlines.

Dasa acquired a majority stake in Fokker as part of a 1993 rescue plan. The shares it bought this week have effectively become worthless due to Fokker's bankruptcy and no money changed hands in the transaction, the Dutch government said.
